title: D15 checks that a citation's FILE exists, never that the file is evidence — proven by mutation
detail: D15's stated purpose: "OD-25 makes a probe output, a saved fixture or a file:line the only acceptable basis for a rank ... it refuses an evidence reference that does not resolve to a file that exists (an unfollowable citation is an invented one, D11's lesson applied to sources)". Its entire assertion is: var p = path.join(EV_DIR, String(ref).split('#')[0]); if (fs.existsSync(p)) evHave++;  MUTATION TEST RUN: I rewrote every one of the 105 refs in docs/design/evidence.json to 'fixtures/investorgain/gmp-live.json' — a 29-key InvestorGain GMP report that contains no registrar, no face value, no EPS, no NSE/BSE/Chittorgarh data at all — and re-ran the gate. Result, verbatim: '[PASS] D15  105 of 387 (field, source) pairs carry evidence that resolves (floor 105).' The file was restored from backup immediately (git status --porcelain docs/design/evidence.json clean). D15 does not check the label, does not check that the fixture even belongs to the cited SOURCE, and does not re-run the mapper. Every one of the wrong matches in F-84 through F-88 passes D15 today, and so would 105 refs pointing at a single unrelated file. The ratchet is a ratchet on path-existence, not on evidence.
recommendation: Make D15 re-run evidence-map.mjs (or read its committed .out.json) and assert three things per pair: (a) the fixture path equals the fixture the mapper recorded, (b) the recorded LABEL is still present in that fixture, (c) the fixture is under the directory owned by the cited source (fixtures/nse/** for NSE, etc.). Keep the existsSync test as the cheapest of the three, not the only one. Add a self-test that flips one ref to a foreign fixture and asserts D15 FAILS — the check that D15 lacked today.

title: The prefix rule reintroduces the exact "PAT Margin" class the mapper's own comment claims to have blocked: financial_statements.pat is evidenced by "P/E (x)"
detail: The mapper's comment: "A label may not carry a token that CHANGES what the number is. 'PAT Margin' contains every token of `pat` and is a different quantity ... Evidence for the wrong quantity is the most expensive kind of wrong, because it looks right." The committed output says: financial_statements.pat | CG | how='all tokens in label' | label='P/E (x)' | fixture=chittorgarh/vinod-texworld-ltd.html | label_extras=[]. ROOT CAUSE, re-derived from the code: hasToken accepts (a.startsWith(t) && a.length - t.length <= 2). The synonym 'pat' therefore matches the one-letter label token 'p' from "P/E (x)" (3-1=2). MEANING_CHANGERS blocks 'margin' but "P/E (x)" tokenises to ['p','e','x'] and carries no blocked word, so the guard never fires. The same rule makes 'eps'~'e' and 'pbv'~'p'. This is not a lone slip; the same matcher produced four more wrong-QUANTITY pairs I checked: ipo_valuation.price_cap | CG | 'Market Cap at Offer Price' (a Rs139 price cap evidenced by Rs4,516.07 Cr market cap); ipo_demand_graph.is_cut_off | NSE | 'Cut-off time for UPI Mandate Confirmation' and the identical BSE key (a boolean bid-at-cut-off flag evidenced by a clock time); subscriptions.retail_subscription | NSE | 'Maximum Subscription Amount for Retail Investor' sample "Rs. 2,00,000" (a subscription multiple evidenced by a static regulatory cap — and the SAME label is the correct evidence for ipo_details.max_retail_subscription, so one label backs two columns that are different things); ipos.segment | NSE | 'series' sample "EQ" (MAINBOARD/SME evidenced by a trading series). SECOND MECHANISM, same matcher: MEANING_CHANGERS includes 'peer', so a label containing "peer" is REJECTED as an extra token — which makes it structurally impossible for a peer_companies.* column to be evidenced by a peer-table label, and forces every peer column onto the ISSUER's own row instead: peer_companies.eps | CG | 'EPS (Rs)', peer_companies.ronw | CG | 'RoNW', peer_companies.eps | DOC | 'eps_basic_by_fy'. The guard is one-directional and inverts its own intent for that table.
where: docs/design/probes/evidence-map.mjs:214-219 (hasToken), :236-247 (MEANING_CHANGERS); docs/design/probes/evidence-map.out.json (pairs for financial_statements.pat, ipo_valuation.price_cap, ipo_demand_graph.is_cut_off, subscriptions.retail_subscription, ipos.segment, peer_companies.*)
recommendation: Drop the prefix tolerance for label tokens shorter than 3 characters (a 1-2 char token can never disambiguate a quantity). Make MEANING_CHANGERS symmetric: if the COLUMN carries a qualifier the label lacks (peer, diluted, weighted, anchor, retail) that is as disqualifying as the reverse. Add a regression fixture asserting `pat` does NOT match "P/E (x)" and that peer_companies.eps does not match the issuer "EPS" row — the mapper has now been caught by three successive reviews on the same class, so the guard needs a test, not another comment.

title: ipos.issue_size (a rupee amount) is evidenced by BSE's share COUNT — the named historical "share counts stored as rupees" defect, now inside the evidence layer
detail: Committed pair: ipos.issue_size | BSE | how='all tokens in label' | label='Issue_Size_No_of_shares' | sample='36912363' | fixture=bse/GetMkt_ISSUE_BBS_IPO-7950.json. RE-DERIVED from the fixture: I enumerated every key of IPONO_0[0] matching /size|amount|price|issue/i. The complete list is Issue_Period, Post_Issue_Modification, Issue_Size_No_of_shares, Price_Band, Price_Band_Advertisement, Tick_Size, Registrar_issue_share_Transfer_Agents_Depository. There is NO rupee-denominated issue-size key in the BSE payload at all. So the evidence recorded for "BSE carries ipos.issue_size" is a count of 36,912,363 shares, and the label itself says _No_of_shares. This is precisely the defect class the brief names as the reason this review exists (share counts stored as rupees), reappearing one layer up: the rank is now backed by a citation that would licence writing a share count into an amount column. ipo_details.ofs_issue | BSE is evidenced by the SAME key, which is wrong twice — wrong unit and wrong entity (total issue size is not the offer-for-sale component).
recommendation: Teach the matcher units: a label containing no_of_shares/shares/quantity may not evidence a column classed as an amount in section 5.2's 37-amount-column list (D13 already knows which columns are amounts — reuse that list). Re-verdict ipos.issue_size|BSE and ipo_details.ofs_issue|BSE as UNPROVEN with the reason "BSE carries the share count only", and lower the floor with a stated reason as the spec's own comment requires.

title: ipos.close_date is evidenced by the financial table's "Period Ended" header while the real "Close date" label sits in the same file
detail: Committed pair: ipos.close_date | CG | label='Period Ended' | sample='31 Mar 2026 | 31 Mar 2025 | 31 Mar 2024' | fixture=chittorgarh/asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd.html. RE-DERIVED: I grepped that label out of the fixture. "Period Ended" is the <th> of the financial summary table — the row set under it is Assets 4,460.85 / Total Income 785.08 / Profit After Tax 407.84 / EBITDA 588.93 / NET Worth 3,079.39 / Reserves and Surplus / Total Borrowing, with the footer "Amount in Rs Crore". Those three dates are fiscal year-ends, not the IPO's bidding close. The same fixture DOES contain the correct label — grep -o -i "Close date" returns two hits. The wrong one won because match() returns the FIRST row that satisfies the token test (for (const r of rows) { ... return {...r}; }) with no scoring and no preference for the closer label; "Period Ended" simply appears earlier in DOM row order. Every CARRIES verdict in the file is therefore first-match, not best-match, and the recorded label is the first plausible one rather than the right one. This is the same shape as the earlier round's "live IPO dates match Chittorgarh exactly" claim: a date cited against a date-shaped thing that is a different date.
recommendation: Score candidates instead of returning the first: prefer exact-label, then fewest label_extras, then shortest label; on a tie of two or more scoring candidates record AMBIGUOUS with both labels rather than picking one. At minimum, when a label whose flattened form equals the column name exists anywhere in the index, it must win over a token-overlap match elsewhere in the same fixture.

title: One Chittorgarh cell labelled "Name" is the recorded evidence for three different entities, and its own sample shows it is a table header row
detail: Three committed pairs share one label and one fixture: promoters.name | CG | label='Name', registrars.name | CG | label='Name', ipo_intermediaries.name | CG | label='Name' — all with sample='Category | No. of Shares Offered | Amount ( cr.)', all how='exact label', all from chittorgarh/asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd.html. The sample is the mapper's own record of the cells that FOLLOW the label in that row; "Category | No. of Shares Offered | Amount ( cr.)" is a row of column headings from the reservation/quota table, not a person's or a firm's name. So the evidence says: a cell reading "Name" whose neighbours are three column captions proves that Chittorgarh carries the promoter name, the registrar name and the intermediary name. It proves none of them — a label that resolves to three mutually exclusive entities identifies zero. This survived the round-4 fix that removed nav-link matches because that fix only excluded short page-text lines; a bare <th>Name</th> inside a real table passes the current filter (label.length <= 45 && !label.includes('?')) untouched.
recommendation: Reject any CARRIES where the same (source, label) is claimed by two or more distinct table.column pairs whose table differs — record all of them as AMBIGUOUS. Separately, drop generic one-word labels (Name, Value, Type, Total, Amount) from the CG index unless qualified by the enclosing table's caption; index the caption + cell as a compound label so "Promoter Holding - Name" and "Registrar - Name" are distinguishable.

title: The offer document's PROMOTER is cited as the registrar and as the intermediary; the issuer's compliance-officer email is cited as the registrar's email
detail: Four committed pairs, all how='all tokens in label', all from extraction/asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd-PRICE_BAND_AD.json: registrars.name | DOC | label='promoter_name' | sample='Avenue India Resurgence Pte. Ltd'; ipo_intermediaries.name | DOC | label='promoter_name' (same value); registrars.email | DOC | label='compliance_officer_email' | sample='cs@arcil.co.in'; ipo_intermediaries.email | DOC | label='compliance_officer_email' (same value). Avenue India Resurgence Pte. Ltd is a private-equity promoter selling shares. The registrar for this IPO is MUFG Intime India Private Limited — a fact the SAME probe output records correctly two rows away (ipos.registrar | NSE | label='Name of the Registrar' | sample='MUFG Intime India Private Limited' and ipos.registrar | BSE | label='Registrar'). So the evidence file simultaneously holds the right registrar from NSE/BSE and asserts the offer document proves the registrar is the promoter. cs@arcil.co.in is the ISSUER's own company-secretary address; citing it as the registrar's contact would, if implemented, route investor allotment queries to the issuer. This is the identical class to the already-caught ipos.registrar -> plausibility-check match: the matcher has no concept of which ENTITY a column belongs to, only which words appear.
recommendation: Add an entity gate before the token test: derive the entity prefix from the table name (registrars -> registrar/rta, promoters -> promoter, ipo_intermediaries -> the intermediary role, anchor_investors -> anchor) and require the label to carry that entity token, or record UNPROVEN. promoter_name must never be able to evidence a row in registrars. Re-run and re-state the floor.

title: The A.0 table introduced as machine-generated disagrees with the machine on three of seven rows, and the headline total is stale by nine
detail: The section says: "This round did it mechanically, and the numbers below are generated by `probes/evidence-map.mjs` rather than counted by a person", then "**114 of 386 pairs are backed by a payload we hold.** Check **D15** enforces that number as a ratchet", then "**What the other 272 mean** ...", and closes "Tightening it to full-token matches ... cut the total to 114". I re-ran node docs/design/probes/evidence-map.mjs; the output is byte-identical to the committed .out.json except the timestamp, and prints: pairs: {"UNPROVEN":272,"CARRIES":105,"UNPROBED":10} — DOC {48,115}, NSE {15,42}, BSE {12,43}, CG {29,72}, IG {1,0}. The prose table says NSE 19/38, BSE 15/40, CG 31/69 (DOC and IG do match). 105+272+10 = 387, not 386. The spec knows the truth and says so in its own comment: "Lowered once, on purpose and on the record: 114 -> 105 on 2026-09-09" — and D15 prints "105 of 387". So the prose was left at the pre-tightening numbers while the generator, the spec and the gate all moved to the post-tightening ones. Note the internal tell nobody caught: the prose's own "the other 272" is the CURRENT UNPROVEN count, which only adds up against 105, never against 114.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md:2536-2547 (per-source table), :2547 (phrase: 114 of 386 pairs are backed), :2572 (phrase: cut the total to 114) [line numbers as read 2026-09-09; the file is being edited concurrently in this worktree, so grep the quoted phrases]; docs/design/field-source-resolution.spec.mjs:348-357 (EVIDENCE_FLOOR = 105 and the 114 -> 105 note); docs/design/probes/evidence-map.out.json
recommendation: Delete the hand-typed table and total and generate that block from evidence-map.out.json (the design already does this for other counts), or at minimum extend D2 to fail on any of these literals drifting — see F-90. Until then the section's opening sentence ("generated ... rather than counted by a person") is false as written.

title: D2 promises "no generator-owned count is hand-typed into the prose" and inspects exactly two phrase shapes — it passes on the stale numbers of F-89
detail: D2's message on PASS is the unqualified sentence "No generator-owned count is hand-typed into the prose." Its complete implementation is: const handTyped = [[/the (\d+) sourced fields/g, 'plan-row count in prose'], [/\bexactly (\d+)\b(?=[^|]*E-1)/g, 'E-1 count in prose']]; — two regexes for two specific sentences. It examines nothing else. Every generator-owned number in F-89 — "114 of 386 pairs", the per-source columns 19/38, 15/40, 31/69, and "cut the total to 114" — is hand-typed into the prose, is currently WRONG, and D2 reports [PASS] D2 No generator-owned count is hand-typed into the prose. The design's stated standard of proof rests on checks like this one; a check whose PASS line asserts a general property while its body tests two string patterns is the same failure shape as D10c (which the design records as having been decoration twice). It is not that D2 does nothing — it is that its PASS line certifies far more than it looked at, and the gap is where F-89 lived undetected through a round explicitly about verification.
where: docs/design/check-design-consistency.mjs (D2, the handTyped array and its two regexes)
recommendation: Either (a) narrow D2's PASS message to name the two sentences it actually inspects, so the gate stops certifying a property it does not test, or (b) make D2 real: enumerate the counts each probe .out.json owns, scan the prose for those literal integers in the sections that cite that probe, and fail on any mismatch. (b) is the one that would have caught F-89 the day the floor moved 114 -> 105.

title: The SME document-type split that sets the rank-1 order for 173 IPOs has no probe behind it and does not reconcile with the one probe that counts documents
detail: The claim, in the same section that declares its numbers machine-generated: "Measured on production, SME IPOs have **zero PRICE_BAND_AD documents** (mainboard has 12) and one DRHP (mainboard has 18); their document set is dominated by the prospectus (64). So for SME the rank-1 document order is **PROSPECTUS > RHP > CORRIGENDUM > DRHP** ... For 173 SME IPOs — over half the site — the price band, share counts and market cap come from the prospectus." I checked every probe output for a segment x document-type breakdown: grep -o "PRICE_BAND_AD" docs/design/probes/*.out.json returns nothing, and old-document-availability.out.json (the only other document probe) carries keys probe/generated_at/question/method/per_age_target/attempted/obtainable/url_coverage/by_host_and_age/documents — no type counts by segment. The phrase "Measured on production" cites no query, no file:line and no .out.json. The one probe that does count by type, document-store-size.out.json, reports PRICE_BAND_AD: 13 documents across all IPOs — which the stated split (mainboard 12 + SME 0 = 12) does not reach; DRHP 19 reconciles (18+1) and PROSPECTUS 81 leaves mainboard 17 unstated. One of the two numbers is wrong or the populations differ, and nothing in the design says which. This drives a per-segment source-order decision for more than half the site.
recommendation: Add the query as a probe (probes/document-types-by-segment.mjs) that emits the segment x type matrix, cite its .out.json beside the claim, and reconcile the PRICE_BAND_AD count against document-store-size's 13 in the same output (state whether one counts active-only and the other all rows). Until it exists, mark the SME order PROVISIONAL — section 0.0.3's standard of proof does not admit "measured on production" with nothing to open.

title: One number, 52,731,946, is the recorded evidence for four distinct columns, and the other source's evidence for the same IPO's share count is 43% smaller — nothing compares them
detail: For the same IPO (ARCIL) the committed evidence records: ipo_valuation.shares_at_cap | DOC | label='total_offer_shares_at_cap' | sample='52731946'; ipo_valuation.total_shares_at_cap | DOC | 'total_offer_shares_at_cap' | '52731946'; ipo_valuation.ofs_shares | DOC | 'ofs_shares' | '52731946'; anchor_investors.total_shares_offered | DOC | 'total_offer_shares_at_cap' | '52731946'. Four columns that are four different quantities — the total offer, the OFS component, and the anchor allocation — all evidenced by the same figure. If ofs_shares == total_offer_shares_at_cap is truly what the extractor produced, then fresh issue = 0 for this IPO, which makes the design's A7 invariant ("fresh + OFS = total at the same price point", line 629) trivially satisfied and unable to detect anything on this fixture; and an anchor allocation equal to the entire offer is not possible under SEBI's anchor cap. Meanwhile the BSE payload for the same IPO gives Issue_Size_No_of_shares = 36912363 — 43% below the document figure — and that pair is separately recorded as CARRIES (F-85). The mapper records label and fixture per pair and never compares the VALUES two sources give for the same quantity on the same IPO, so a 43% cross-source disagreement and a physically impossible anchor figure both pass as evidence.
recommendation: Add a cross-source consistency pass to the mapper: where two sources are CARRIES for the same column on the same walkthrough IPO, compare the values and record AGREES / DISAGREES(delta) — a DISAGREES pair is a rank finding, not a backed rank. Separately, flag any single (fixture, label) value that backs three or more distinct columns as a suspected extractor collapse and re-read the PDF for that IPO before the floor counts those pairs.
